title: Hugh Hefner’s Ex-Wife Calls Him a ‘True Gentleman’ After His Widow Crystal Harris Urges Jessica Biel to ‘Reconsider’ Playing His Wife
description: Kimberly Hefner, who was married to Hugh Hefner from 1989 until their divorce was finalized in 2010, has taken to social media to share a statement
body:
Kimberly Hefner, who was married to Hugh Hefner from 1989 until their divorce was finalized in 2010, has taken to social media to share a statement in support of her late husband after his former wife, Crystal Harris, alleged she experienced sexual, emotional, financial and physical abuse while married to the Playboy magazine founder. Harris shared her story following the news that Jessica Biel would play a fictional version of Hefner’s wife in the upcoming film “Playmates.”
	

	“I was married to Hef for over 21 years. We shared a lifetime of beautiful memories, raised 2 wonderful sons together, and had a deeply loving bond that remained strong until his passing on September 27th, 2017 and continues with me to this day,” wrote Kimberly. “I often told him if you look up the word gentleman in the dictionary you would find his name and photograph. Hef was in every sense of the word, a true gentleman, kind, loving, generous, philanthropic, and a man of extraordinary character.”


	She continued: “Losing Hef was devastating, and his absence is still deeply felt. I had the privilege of knowing and loving the man behind the public image, and I will always treasure the life and memories we shared. I will always believe the world was a better place because he was in it. I am forever grateful and blessed.”

	Before they tied the knot, Kimberly and Hugh met when she was modeling for Playboy’s Playmate of the Month centerfold. Hugh met Harris at a Halloween party at the Playboy Mansion when she was a 21-year-old college student. She moved into the mansion shortly thereafter and married Hugh in 2012. The two remained together until his death in Sept. 2017, after which Harris published her 2024 memoir “Only Say Good Things: Surviving Playboy and Finding Myself,” in which she revealed her experiences at the mansion.
	

	“Playmates” will revolve around “Elle (Indiana Elle), a 13-year-old know-it-all who considers the Playboy Mansion her second home, and meets Anna (Lily-Rose Depp), one of seven hopefuls vying to be Playmate of the Month,” per the film’s synopsis. “The two form an unlikely friendship and try to help each other get what the other wants most, a magazine cover and a boy.”

	Lorraine Nicholson, the daughter of Jack Nicholson, is writing and directing the Searchlight film. Bill Pullman will star as Hugh.

	See Kimberly’s post below.

schema.headline: Hugh Hefner’s Ex-Wife Calls Him a ‘True Gentleman’ After His Widow Crystal Harris Urges Jessica Biel to ‘Reconsider’ Playing His Wife

title: Quentin Tarantino Play ‘The Popinjay Cavalier,’ Starring Sacha Baron Cohen, to Open on West End in March
description:
Quentin Tarantino‘s first-ever stage play, “The Popinjay Cavalier” starring Sacha Baron Cohen, will open at London’s Phoenix Theatre in March. 

	Wr
body:
Quentin Tarantino‘s first-ever stage play, “The Popinjay Cavalier” starring Sacha Baron Cohen, will open at London’s Phoenix Theatre in March. 

	Written and directed by Tarantino, the play — described as a “swashbuckling comedy” — will hold previews from Feb. 23, with opening night set for March 18. It’s set to run for three months, closing on June 13. Tickets will go on sale via the play’s website at 9 a.m. BST on Monday, starting at just £25. 
	

	“I’m keen with anticipation to give the West End a great night out,” Tarantino said in a statement.


	Set in 1830s Europe, “The Popinjay Cavalier” is a “rambunctious comedy of deception and disguise inspired by the grand swashbuckling epics of stage and screen,” as the play’s synopsis reads. “A sweeping celebration of theatre and its heightened romance, told with Tarantino’s signature style and unmistakable wit, ‘The Popinjay Cavalier’ is inspired by the classic swashbuckler genre of old Hollywood, including the writings of George Bruce, Ernst Vajda and Jesse Lasky Jr.” 

	Added Baron Cohen, whose casting was first revealed last month: “Quentin called, I said yes before he even got to say his first ‘motherf—er’. When the best director in the world calls, you don’t ask questions. I am beyond delighted that we will be losing our West End virginity together, I have made him promise not to be gentle.”

	Producers Tom Rothman, chairman and CEO of Sony Pictures Entertainment’s Motion Picture group, and Sonia Friedman said it is a “joy and an honor to be developing this play with Quentin — and absolutely quite an adventure.”
	

	They continued, “How lucky we are that one of the great storytellers of our time has chosen to make his theatrical debut. To see Quentin in action in a rehearsal room is extraordinary. His delight in working with actors, fencers, acrobats, musicians and our creative team is infectious, and there is such pleasure in hearing his delicious language come alive and discovering what his world can become on stage.”

	The duo went on to say that Baron Cohen is a “fearless, brilliantly inventive actor with the wit, mischief and daring this role demands. We feel immensely fortunate to be producing this show. Audiences are in for a tremendous treat.”

	The creative team joining Tarantino includes scenic and costume designer Tom Pye, lighting designer Natasha Chivers, sound designer Ian Dickinson, fight director Philip d’Orleans and action coordinator Sam Lyon-Behan, with music by Tim Phillips and casting by Jim Carnahan, CSA. 

	Further casting will be announced at a later date.

schema.headline: Quentin Tarantino Play ‘The Popinjay Cavalier,’ Starring Sacha Baron Cohen, to Open on West End in March

title: After Kelly Clarkson Slams Brooklyn Novelty Store, Shop Says the ‘One-of-a-Kind’ Singing Bird She Wanted Wasn’t Actually For Sale
description: After Kelly Clarkson took to X on Saturday to share her experience “being treated like Julia Roberts” in “Pretty Woman” during a visit to Art of Pla
body:
After Kelly Clarkson took to X on Saturday to share her experience “being treated like Julia Roberts” in “Pretty Woman” during a visit to Art of Play, a novelty shop in Brooklyn, the local business is responding to her claims, saying it has received “widespread outrage” since and explaining that the item she wanted to buy — a bird permanently fixed to the store’s wall– was not actually for sale.

	In her initial tweet, which has garnered nearly 260,000 likes and 32.2 million views, the singer wrote that she had driven to the store, which she thought “looked really rad and had a few things in mind to buy.” She continued, writing that she “literally was looked at as if I couldn’t afford it and was told he could find something comparable for me. Wow, dude. You’re an idiot and just lost a huge sale.” She then named the store and told her fans to visit if they “enjoy being treated like Julia Roberts character in Pretty Woman,” accompanied by a thumbs-down emoji.
	

	On Sunday, the business posted a multi-slide carousel to the store’s Instagram account sharing their side of the story. They began by clarifying that the item Clarkson inquired about purchasing was “a one-of-a-kind singing and dancing bird automaton who plays an important role in the magic shows we host here.” “Molly is permanently attached to the wall and isn’t for sale. However, the negative experience Kelly described on Twitter would resonate with anyone who has ever felt judged in a shop,” the caption read.

	The business continued to note that “whether someone comes in to make a purchase or simply look around for a while, they are equally welcome. We greet everyone who walks in the door with the invitation to ‘pick things up and play.’ And they do, many stay for hours enjoying our puzzles, games and toys.”
	

	Art of Play also acknowledged the significant backlash they’ve been receiving since Clarkson’s statement, before quoting the singer and concluding the message.

	“Imagine our surprise when our small local business was suddenly attacked by 8 million people who have never visited our store. It’s been a surreal experience to be the focus of such widespread outrage after just one mention by a celebrity. Thanks to all our friends for their support and welcome to all the curious folks who have discovered us amidst the drama. We’re going to keep our heads down and hopefully, we can clear things up with Kelly someday. As a talented popular singer once said ‘what doesn’t kill you makes you stronger.'”

	In a Feb. 2025 Instagram post’s caption, the business wrote that Molly is the store’s “beloved shop bird” and “mascot,” and she is one of the few items in Art of Play that has a “Do Not Touch” sign.  

	See the full posts below.

title: John Stamos Addresses Mike Love’s Health as Beach Boys Concert Footage Raises Concerns: ‘We Don’t Know What the Future Holds — We Have Tonight’
description: Following many Beach Boys fans and followers expressing concern for Mike Love after seeing footage from the group’s Saturday night show in Cincinnat
body:
Following many Beach Boys fans and followers expressing concern for Mike Love after seeing footage from the group’s Saturday night show in Cincinnati, John Stamos has stepped in with a statement acknowledging that Love is in poor health as they are doing these shows and suggesting that his longtime friend’s time on stage may be nearing an end.

	“I’ve played with Mike for 41 years. I never imagined how deeply it would affect me to see someone larger than life face something so human and fragile,” Stamos said in his Instagram post, managing expectations on his way to performing with the Beach Boys at a show scheduled for Sunday at Nashville’s Ryman Auditorium.
	

	“We hope he’ll be doing what he loves for years to come, but we don’t know what the future holds. We have tonight,” Stamos said. The actor-musician added, “The Mike Love we see tonight may not be exactly the Mike we’ve always known. But he’s still every bit the Mike we love.” (Scroll down to read Stamos’ complete statement.)


	The Beach Boys had been off the road since July, canceling several months of dates as Love addressed health concerns, with a pledge to take up where they left off. More gigs kept being canceled, one by one, until the group finally resumed action, first with a private performance and then a return to public touring with Saturday’s Cincinnati show. But many were alarmed by what they saw in fan-posted video, with Love appearing much weaker and less engaged than he was even in July’s shows. 

	The frontman for the group for the last six and a half decades remained seated and largely motionless for the entire show in Ohio, not taking any of the many lead vocals he was still doing when the Beach Boys performed for three nights at the Hollywood Bowl in July. One short clip that quickly circulated on social media showed Stamos urging Love to do some hand gestures from his seat, and the Beach Boys’ mainstay gamely complying, but without much apparent energy, before going back to sitting in place.
	

	The Nashville show is the last one on the Beach Boys’ itinerary until mid-November, when they are scheduled to play in Orlando Nov. 11 and Bristol Nov. 13. After that, they just have one gig publicly announced for 2027, in contrast to the usual robust touring schedule they would usually have announced by this time, leading fans to wonder if they really may be prepared to be winding up Love’s time fronting the group.

	Coincidentally, across the country, another Beach Boys mainstay from the beginning, Al Jardine, is doing a concert Sunday night in which guest appearances have been promised by two other historical Beach Boys members, Bruce Johnston (who until a few months ago was still part of Love’s touring unit) and David Marks.


	John Stamos’ complete statement from Sunday afternoon: 

	I’m boarding a plane to Nashville to play with the Beach Boys at the Ryman Auditorium, struggling to put my feelings into words.My beloved friend, father figure, musical hero and mentor, Mike Love, is facing serious health challenges. We hope he’ll be doing what he loves for years to come, but we don’t know what the future holds. We have tonight.Mike is a fighter. Despite doctors, family and friends urging him to focus on his health, he insists on being on stage. He says he needs his band, the audience, his friends and drummer surrounding him to lift him up.I’ve played with Mike for 41 years. I never imagined how deeply it would affect me to see someone larger than life face something so human and fragile.The Mike Love we see tonight may not be exactly the Mike we’ve always known. But he’s still every bit the Mike we love.His lyrics, optimism, unforgettable hooks and more than 7,000 concerts have brought joy to generations. What he’s given me personally is immeasurable.Forty-one years of stages, airplanes, hotel rooms, laughter and moments nobody else saw. He married Caitlin and me. He’s shared experiences with my family, and now my son.Mike didn’t just give me a place in his band. He gave me a place in his life.He taught me how to entertain, hold a stage, connect with an audience and make people feel something. I carry those lessons everywhere. He’s made me a better musician, entertainer and man.This life with Mike and the Beach Boys has become part of my identity. I’ve felt entrusted with being a steward of this extraordinary music, carrying it to new generations.Tonight, at the Ryman, sharing the stage with Mike, I want to be completely present. Hear every harmony, familiar joke and cheer. Feel that first chord hit and watch age, illness and time disappear. Just a bunch of guys making music together.Maybe the hardest part of loving someone is becoming so accustomed to the miracle of having them there that you forget it’s a miracle at all.Tonight, I won’t forget.I want to cherish every second without feeling those seconds slipping away.That’s what I’m giving him.We don’t know what tomorrow brings. But we have tonight.

schema.headline: John Stamos Addresses Mike Love’s Health as Beach Boys Concert Footage Raises Concerns: ‘We Don’t Know What the Future Holds — We Have Tonight’

title: ‘Animals’ Star Luis Gerardo Méndez on Working With Ben Affleck and Speaking Out About Immigration: ‘You Could Be Next’
description: When Luis Gerardo Méndez got a call from his agents that Ben Affleck wanted to cast him in “Animals,” he was surprised the Oscar winner even knew wh
body:
When Luis Gerardo Méndez got a call from his agents that Ben Affleck wanted to cast him in “Animals,” he was surprised the Oscar winner even knew who he was.

	“They sent me the script, and it had a very beautiful note at the end from Ben, just saying like, ‘Hey, Luis, I really want you to be in the movie. This script is not ready. I’m gonna do a rewrite specifically about your character, so I’m gonna call you around Christmas because I would love to hear your thoughts,’” Méndez tells me.
	

	They didn’t meet in person until the first day of rehearsals.


	“Ben saw me and he came to me with his massive Batman back and hugged me, and he started screaming to everyone like, ‘This guy is the best actor in Mexico. He’s incredible!’” says Méndez, who first gained fame in his native Mexico with his starring role in the 2013 comedy “The Noble Family.” “He brought me to his office and he started speaking like nonstop for an hour about me and how excited he was to work with me. At the end I was like, ‘Ben, can I ask you something? Why are you so excited to work with me?’ And he was like, ‘“Narcos: Mexico.” Your character is incredible. I was watching “Narcos,” and I called Matt [Damon, who was originally supposed to star in the film] and said, ‘Hey, dude, are you watching “Narcos?” The cop. We need to get the cop.’”

	Méndez starred in the third season of the Netflix series “Narcos: Mexico” in 2021 as corrupt cop Victor Tapia.

	Affleck stars in “Animals” — he also directed the film and co-wrote the script — as a businessman running for Los Angeles mayor when he and his wife (Kerry Washington) receive a phone call saying that their son Denny (Christopher Woodley) has been kidnapped.
	

	Méndez plays Ramon, the undocumented Mexican boyfriend of the couple’s housekeeper (Adriana Paz), who finds himself unexpectedly thrust into trying to resolve the kidnapping when things take a drastic turn. 

	As for Affleck’s script changes for Ramon, Méndez says, “It was so magical because it was like if Ben had read my mind, like all the things that I thought about the character that were missing, about the proper representation, about the proper way of speaking of the characters … everything was there.”

	While the film is meant to entertain, Méndez hopes it also fosters conversations around immigration.

	“What I want the audiences to think about for a second is: no one leaves their homes because they want to,” he says. “They leave it because they’re running away from violence, from political persecution. We need to understand that. The vast majority of the immigrants, not just in the U.S. but in the whole world, they just want to work and they’re very hard workers. They just want to do the right thing like our characters in the movie. They’re taking the biggest risks with the least protection. They’re doing the right stuff in a system that won’t allow them to shine or to be heroes.”

	Méndez splits his time between Los Angeles and Mexico City. He also travels the globe as a goodwill ambassador for UNHCR (Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees).

	Méndez chokes up when asked about ICE. “To hear about these families getting separated, it’s really hard for me to speak about it, especially with what happened yesterday here in New York,” he says in reference to the recent ICE shooting of 28-year-old Oscar Belgal. “I feel like no matter what your immigration status is, no one should lose their dignity. It’s as simple as that.”

	He also warns about global warming’s effect on immigration. “We’re going to see massive amounts of people moving, leaving. We’re seeing it already in California,” Méndez explains. “We don’t know if tomorrow we’re going to be the ones migrating. No one has any certainty about that. We must understand that. We must be welcoming because we don’t know what’s going to happen in the next 20 or 30 years. It’s about empathy and also about you could be next, we could be next.”

schema.headline: ‘Animals’ Star Luis Gerardo Méndez on Working With Ben Affleck and Speaking Out About Immigration: ‘You Could Be Next’

title: Taylor Swift Spends Her 100th Week at No. 1 on the Billboard 200, as ‘Life of a Showgirl’ Stays on Top in Week 2 of ‘Encore’ Rebound
description: Taylor Swift is fond of the number 13, but here’s betting she also considers the numeral 100 lucky, too. She can now celebrate having 100 weeks at N
body:
Taylor Swift is fond of the number 13, but here’s betting she also considers the numeral 100 lucky, too. She can now celebrate having 100 weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 chart, for all of her albums combined, further extending a record among solo artists that will be difficult for anyone to catch up with in our lifetimes.

	She hit the magic 100 mark by having “The Life of a Showgirl” hold on at No. 1 for a second straight week, bolstered by the release of ax extended edition. This bonus-filled version with four new tracks, titled “The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore,” counts alongside the original edition for chart calculation purposes, so “Showgirl” is officially enjoying a 14th week at No. 1.
	

	As Billboard points out, Swift has no real rivals among solo artists when it comes to those 100 weeks atop the chart. The nearest runner-up is Elvis Presley, who doesn’t stand in too much danger of being able to add very many more No. 1 weeks to his total of 67. The nearest runner-up among living artists is Garth Brooks, with just over half Swift’s number, at 52. However, she doesn’t have the all-time record when it comes to all artists: That belongs to the Beatles, who have 132 collective weeks at No. 1. Based on her recent chart runs, Swift has the potential to overtake the Beatles with just 2-3 more original album releases.


	Speaking of the Beatles, they joined her in the top 10 this week. “Rubber Soul” reenters the chart at No. 4, thanks to a reissue campaign that includes a boxed set as well as remastered editions of the original album. This is the first time the 60-year-old album has been in the top 10 since April 1966. (It last charted on the overall Billboard 200 in January 2016.)
	

	The other fresh action in the top 10 comes from two more rebounding albums — which, along with the big returns for Swift and the Beatles, makes for four albums out of 10 that are suddenly back in the upper ranks because of a re-release or deluxe edition. Drake‘s “Habibti” jumps up from No. 116 to No. 2 on the strength of a reissue with four new tracks. Mac Miller’s “The Divine Feminine” jumps from No. 159 to No. 10 because of a 10th anniversary celebration edition. 

	“The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore” was able to stay comfortably on top with 93,000 equivalent units, down 46% from what the extended version came out of the gate with last week.

	The Drake album was in at No. 2 with 71,000 units. Olivia Rodrigo’s “You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love” continued its winning streak with 66,000 units, good for No. 3. At No. 4, the Beatles used those rubber soles to bounce up to 58,000 units after all these years.

	Rounding out the top 10 are Morgan Wallen’s “I’m the Problem” at No. 5 (55,000 units), Ella Langley’s “Dandelion” at No. 6 (54,000), Noah Kahan’s “The Great Divide” at No. 7 (46,000), Olivia Dean’s “The Art of Loving” at No. 8 (35,000), Kahan’s “Stick Season” at No. 9 (with 33,000) and Miller’s 10-year-old “Divine Feminine” (bolstered by three added tracks) at No. 10 (33,000)

title: Why Disney’s Kids & Family Division Is Working With Creators Like Dhar Mann and Nastya: We Need to ‘Meet Kids Where They Are’
description: During a panel discussion at MipJunior in Cannes on Sunday, Ayo Davis, president of Disney’s Kids & Family division, reflected on how the studio was
body:
During a panel discussion at MipJunior in Cannes on Sunday, Ayo Davis, president of Disney’s Kids & Family division, reflected on how the studio was responding to the disruption in viewing habits among younger viewers, including working with some of the same creators who are contributing to that disruption.

	“I think we can all probably acknowledge that there’s been a lot of disruption, especially in the kids space,” Davis said. “We talk about it a lot. Kids are watching anything and everything. I experience it in my own home with a 12 year old. I like to say, they’re watching everything from ‘Bluey’ to ‘Squid Game.’ So it was clear that we had to activate quickly. This audience is really important to us. We had to step outside of ourselves and take a look at how we were approaching our strategy.”
	

	She added, “So what did that mean? It meant looking at how we told stories with our beloved franchises, how we were connecting with our audience around originals, how we were actually connecting with our audience through new formats, and taking a look at how our content showed up across our platforms – we couldn’t do it the same anymore – and really thinking about how we were working with our partners across the industry. Ultimately, we had to really think about how we were going to connect with our audiences through stories that were fresh, that were relevant, authentic for them, while keeping them connected and growing with the brand.”


	Davis added later, “It’s easy to rinse and repeat, but I think in order to evolve and be able to expand – especially at a company that has such a rich history and legacy – you have to be willing to take chances, you have to be willing to expand, and you have to love what you do because you’re going to be pivoting on a regular basis in order to try to meet kids where they are.”
	

	Working With CreatorsThe Disney execs on the panel spoke about how the studio works with creators, such as Nastya and Dhar Mann, who delivered the opening keynote at Mipcom on Sunday.

	“Creators are important. We know that they’re important to our audience. It is literally where they are engaging all day long,” Davis said. “The thing to highlight is that we’re not just connecting with creators for creators’ sake, right? We are connecting with creators that actually bring something to the table, that actually align to our values, and the way we are telling our stories.”

	She added, “Dhar Mann and Nastya are great examples of that. What I am excited about with Dhar Mann is that at its core, his stories are about good and evil, and so we took the thematic around good and evil, which is what we do so well, and the teams have found such great ways to apply the storytelling through those core themes that are so universal.”

	Alyssa Sapire, head of original programming and strategy at preschool content brand Disney Jr., said, “Nastya is, as most know, hugely popular with preschoolers. What she does is she really leans into imaginative play, which really speaks to so much of what is important for preschoolers and what we infuse in our storytelling.”

	Charlie Andrews, executive VP, live action, Disney Kids & Family, said he was also working with Nastya. “Nastya is also, you know, ageing and her interests are changing, so [we are looking to create] content that is also for herself and her demo as they age with her on the live-action side. So we’re really strategic on that.”

	He added, “We just got the scripts for the two series we’ve greenlit with Dhar Mann. They are excellent. They meet kids where they are, just from a dialogue perspective. Everything is so 2026. Maybe it’s already 2027. That’s how ahead of the curve he is and meeting kids exactly where they are, and it’s so refreshing to read, but still has those incredible Disney tenets of friendship and fantasy and magic and wonder, wish fulfilment.”

	Zack Olin, senior VP, development and current series at Disney Television Animation, Disney Kids & Family, said, “Our goal hasn’t changed, which has consistently been: We want to be in business with the world’s best storytellers. We have to listen to our audience because they are really responding to these storytellers.”
	

	Keep It ShortGino Guzzardo, VP, multiplatform content at Disney Kids & Family, spoke about the importance of short-form content to Disney. “Some people say that it was all started by a mouse. I would counter it was all started by a short. So, shorts are very much in Disney’s DNA. It’s what we’ve always done, and cut to today, it is a multifaceted, multi-platform, fractured media landscape, but we’re still following that same tradition of using shorts to get our characters out there to as many screens as possible. If it has a screen on it, we can throw a short on it. We can get our characters out there where people want to watch.

	“A recent example of that is we have a new anthology, a short-film series called ‘Locker Diaries.’ So these are vertical shorts shot through characters’ lockers. Thankfully, a lot of our properties have high-school hallways in them. It feels organic. There’s a reason for being. It gives you a real immersive experience into a character’s world. You get to know them.”

	Fresh Original ContentOne aspect to the studio’s approach to kids content that the Disney execs on the panel were keen to emphasize was the importance of fresh original content, alongside the legacy franchises.

	Sapire said, “We’re always looking for new stories, new storytellers, new formats based on what we know about preschoolers. We’re all pretty obsessed with knowing our audiences well, their passions, their interests, and, for preschoolers specifically, it’s about knowing where they are developmentally and finding those fresh stories to tell with those relatable, connected themes.”

	She added, “ ‘SuperKitties’ is a great example of that. It has all the indicators of becoming a great franchise for us. The fandom is real. We’re finding kids don’t just love dogs, they adore cats too. Over the last three years, we’ve seen ‘SuperKitties’ grow and build. So, we are in it for the long game and building out the whole ecosystem of 60-minute specials, shorts, a regular long form, and also we’re looking to extend their play with toys and other extensions.”

	Kids Love Vampires and WitchesDavis said that Disney Jr. can be seen as “a gateway” for their audience. “It’s the introduction to the company, the introduction to the characters,” she said.
	

	Andrews added, “My job is to take Alyssa’s demo’s hand and bring them into live action for the first time. She’s saying mermaids, witches, vampires, and I’m like, great, ‘Vampirina’ really worked for you … what about a live-action version? And we had huge success in doing that because we know kids love vampires. They love Vampirina, but then they start ageing, and so when they want to start watching a sitcom five years later, then we have something ready for them, but with the familiar IP they love, with the kind of characters they love, but reinvented for them at that age.”

	He added that it also applied to an original that Disney launched last week, “Coven Academy.” “It’s vampires and witches, and as Alyssa has been pointing out to us for years, those are things that kids love, and they love to watch, and as I bring them into live action, it’s with a little bit more emotion and that authenticity of their relationships and where they are at on an emotional level, and a little more sophisticated storytelling.”

	Olin said that the studio’s animation output was also tailored to the various age groups. “Six to 12 is such an interesting age. It’s where kids are starting to define their own tastes, and there’s a broad spectrum of things that they’re interested in. And, coming out of peak television and more choices than ever, we know we have to deliver choice for audiences,” he said. “So we’ll start with shows like ‘Big City Greens,’ and as they evolve and are seeking out slightly more sophisticated themes or serialization then we’ll follow up with shows like ‘Dragon Striker.’”

	Olin said that their decision-making is shaped by “the necessity to understand the audience.” He added, “It’s not about delivering what we think they want. We have to listen to them and respond to them. I spent a lot of time when I joined the company thinking about the long, successful history of animation at Disney, and just reinforce that if we tell compelling stories, we not only reach the hearts of kids, but we can reach a broad audience, and that’s something that I really aspire to do.”

	Researchers Are the Bosses NowSapire pointed to the importance of research. “From the preschool side, we have touch points with preschoolers literally every week because we have an internal educational resource group, so we go and we sit with kids, we share the stories that we are bringing into our series and getting that direct feedback, having an understanding of what they comprehend. And then we bring that back to our writers, our showrunners, to help them evolve the stories based on that feedback. They are our bosses!” she said with a laugh.

schema.headline: Why Disney’s Kids & Family Division Is Working With Creators Like Dhar Mann and Nastya: We Need to ‘Meet Kids Where They Are’

title: Globo Bets on ‘To Love Is to Care’ at Mipcom as It Ushers ‘Super Drama’ Concept: ‘Titles That Represent the Best of the Brazilian Telenovela Tradition’
description: Brazilian media powerhouse Globo arrives at Mipcom with “To Love is to Care,” its latest primetime telenovela by lauded author Walcyr Carrasco. The
body:
Brazilian media powerhouse Globo arrives at Mipcom with “To Love is to Care,” its latest primetime telenovela by lauded author Walcyr Carrasco. The melodrama stars a roster of some of Brazil’s biggest screen stars, including Chay Suede, Letícia Colin, Tony Ramos and Antônio Fagundes. The market marks Globo’s introduction of the telenovela to the international market following a successful run in its home country.

	“To Love Is to Care” is created and written by veteran Carrasco, an Emmy winner for his hit series “Hidden Truths.” Carrasco created the novela with Claudia Souto, with renowned director Amora Mautner taking over the artistic direction.
	

	The story follows the transformation of Adriana (Colin), a woman shattered by a terrible murder and who discovers the strength to start over, driven by an unquenchable thirst for justice. The story gathers all the classic elements of a successful telenovela: passion, revenge, and a major whodunnit arc. The novela also joins two of Brazil’s most popular actors as a majorly successful romantic pairing, with Colin’s Adriana falling in love with Chay Suede’s idealist lawyer Pedro.


	In a statement, Carrasco said the original idea for the story came from a personal experience. Two years ago, he broke a leg and faced a long recovery process that allowed him to realize the importance of “care, empathy, and human connection.” “I realized how the act of caring transforms both the caregiver and the person being cared for,” he noted. “That experience left a deep impression on me and sparked a desire to tell a story set in that world, one that speaks of solidarity, resilience, and affection.”
	

	Angela Colla, head of international business at Globo, says “To Love is to Care” is one of its “Super Dramas” at Mipcom. These are titles that represent “the best of the Brazilian telenovela tradition combined with Globo’s production excellence.”

	“They are stories that stir emotions, spark conversations across generations, and forge deep connections with audiences that extend far beyond the individual episodes,” adds Colla, who says “To Love Is to Care” brings together all these essential elements: “A strong female lead, a sweeping love story, a compelling mystery that hooks the audience, and universal themes that transcend borders.”



	

					Courtesy of Globo
	



	“It is a project of immense technical and artistic scale, impressing right from the premiere with striking sequences, such as the flood scene, which mobilized a production team of 270 professionals,” she goes on. “It is the kind of story with high potential to engage viewers anywhere in the world.”

	The strength of “To Love Is to Care” can already be observed in its performance in Brazil. In its first 12 weeks, the telenovela reached over 119 million Brazilians. Digital engagement mirrored this success: the hashtag #QuemAmaCuida (“To Love is to Care” in its original title) spent over 13 hours among Worldwide Trending Topics and 97 hours in Brazil’s Trending Topics, while interest in the storyline generated more than 139,000 Google searches since its premiere.

	Colla says the reception from Brazilian audiences confirms “that people continue to look for strong, well-told stories.” “‘To Love Is to Care’ delivered an impactful first chapter that won over the audience from the beginning and has maintained a high level of engagement throughout the plot,” she emphasizes. “The narrative structure brings universal elements that work in different markets: a determined girl who goes after what she wants, a great love story, and the classic mystery of ‘who killed?’”

	“This combination of technical excellence and emotional engagement leaves us very excited and confident that the reception in the international market will also be very positive,” she adds, referring to its upcoming experience Super Dramas at Mipcom, where “To Love Is to Care,” “Anything Goes” and Three Graces” proved early highlights at a Globo Showcase held Sunday evening in Cannes .

schema.headline: Globo Bets on ‘To Love Is to Care’ at Mipcom as It Ushers ‘Super Drama’ Concept: ‘Titles That Represent the Best of the Brazilian Telenovela Tradition’

title: ‘Artemis Fowl’ Animated TV Show Set at Disney
description:
Artemis Fowl is coming to TV.

	An animated series adaptation of the bestselling book franchise has been greenlit for Disney Channel and Disney+. Au
body:
Artemis Fowl is coming to TV.

	An animated series adaptation of the bestselling book franchise has been greenlit for Disney Channel and Disney+. Author Eoin Colfer announced the news during the “25 Years of Artemis Fowl” panel at New York Comic Con.

	Colfer will serve as an executive producer of the series, which follows the 13-year-old genius Artemis Fowl, who “uncovers an underground world of armed and dangerous — and surprisingly high-tech — fairies as he launches a plan to capture one and steal its magic to heal his dying mom and save his family,” per the logline.
	

	The first “Artemis Fowl” book was published in 2001, and Colfer followed it up with 10 additional novels, the latest of which came out in 2021. The series has sold more than 35 million copies worldwide and has been translated in 48 languages.


	This isn’t the first time the child prodigy has graced the screen. A live-action film adaptation based on the first book debuted on Disney+ in 2020 to negative reviews. The movie was removed from the streaming service in 2023.

	“For more than two decades, Eoin Colfer’s ‘Artemis Fowl’ books have captivated readers around the world with unforgettable characters, imaginative world-building, and gripping adventures,” said Ayo Davis, president of Disney Kids & Family. “Bringing this beloved franchise to life as an animated series gives us the opportunity to introduce a new generation to Artemis’ world while honoring the longtime fans who have cherished these stories for years.”

	Colfer said, “I am proud and delighted to be part of the formidable team that is putting the ‘Artemis Fowl’ animation on screen. Everyone is so talented and so positive that I feel certain the fairy world is in excellent hands.”
	

	The “Artemis Fowl” series is also executive produced by Ben Juwono and Colleen Evanson.

title: Sally Field Was Like a ‘Mother Figure’ While Filming ‘Mrs. Doubtfire,’ Says Star Matthew Lawrence: ‘We Really Became a Family Unit’
description:
Matthew Lawrence is reflecting on his experience filming “Mrs. Doubtfire,” where he played Sally Field and Robin Williams’ son. 

	The 1993 film fol
body:
Matthew Lawrence is reflecting on his experience filming “Mrs. Doubtfire,” where he played Sally Field and Robin Williams’ son. 

	The 1993 film followed Williams as Daniel, a father who disguises himself as the titular Scottish nanny for his three children — played by Lawrence, Lisa Jakub and Mara Wilson — to prove to his estranged wife, Miranda (Field), that he has matured.


	“We really became a family unit on that set,” Lawrence told Entertainment Weekly about working with his on-screen parents and Pierce Brosnan, who played the boyfriend of Field’s character.
	

	Lawrence shared that, even before rehearsals began, the cast dedicated time to getting to know each other, “so [Field] kind of really became another mother figure.”


	The actor was just 12 when filming the movie and recalled that Field was “so sweet” during the experience, and “she was so caring, so kind. I don’t know how anybody could have anything bad to say about the lady… She was great.”

	As a child actor, Lawrence revealed Field, Williams and Brosnan “neither treated me and talked down to me as a child, nor did they overexpose me to the adult world.”

	The trio of adult actors “walked a line” that was “absolutely wonderful,” making it “one of those incredible, once-in-a-lifetime experiences,” Lawrence recalled, adding that “Sally in particular… she was amazing.”

	Lawrence has continued to occasionally run into Field over the past three decades since “Mrs. Doubtfire” premiered. “She’s always great,” he said. Earlier this year, the actor published a graphic novel, “The Lawrence Brothers Detective Agency,” with his real-life brothers, which included a tribute to Field and Williams.

title: Indigo Girls Mourn Death of Tour Bus Driver After Fatal Crash
description:
Indigo Girls
                          Mourning Beloved Tour Bus Driver After Fatal Crash
body:
Indigo Girls
                          Mourning Beloved Tour Bus Driver After Fatal Crash
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 11, 2026
                            3:31 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The Indigo Girls are mourning a heartbreaking loss on the road ... their longtime tour bus driver was killed in a crash in South Carolina, forcing the folk-rock duo to cancel upcoming shows.
      
    
            The driver -- identified by the band as Kirk -- was behind the wheel Friday morning when the bus slammed into a disabled tractor-trailer on Interstate 20 around 6 AM, according to authorities.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Kirk was the only person on the bus at the time ... neither Indigo Girls members Amy Ray and Emily Saliers nor any of their crew were onboard.
      

            The cause of the crash remains under investigation.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The "Closer to Fine" singers addressed the tragedy in an emotional statement ... saying Kirk had safely driven them thousands of miles over the years and had become a beloved part of their touring family.
      
    
            They wrote, "He was a joyful constant in our lives, and we will miss him dearly."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The duo canceled their Saturday show in Myrtle Beach, South Carolina, and postponed Sunday's performance in Wilmington, North Carolina ... with decisions on additional tour dates still to come.
      
    
            Amy and Emily say they plan to return to the road when they're ready ... but for now, they're remembering the man who helped make their shows possible night after night.

description:
Cornell University
                          Homecoming Concert Cancelled

body:
Cornell University
                          Homecoming Concert Cancelled
                          Students Stand By Jane Doe
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 11, 2026
                            9:07 AM PDT
                                                                            
              
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Cornell University’s homecoming concert has been canceled amid the school's sexual assault scandal, as students rally in support of the alleged victim, identified as Jane Doe.
      
    
            The Cornell Concerts Commission announced it's pulling the plug on its planned Homecoming Concert featuring indie-pop duo Between Friends, which had been scheduled for October 17 at Barton Hall.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The student-run group says the decision comes as it calls on Cornell's administration to do more to support survivors of sexual violence ... saying in a statement to social media, "The Cornell Concert Commission is a student-run organization and, as students, we stand with Jane Doe and all survivors of sexual violence."
      

            The cancellation comes as Cornell faces mounting backlash over its handling of allegations stemming from an alleged 2024 gang rape at the university's Chi Phi fraternity house.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            As TMZ previously reported, we obtained text messages that offer additional insight into the case and the allegations that have rocked the university.
      
    
            In a text chain between one of the accused students Jonathan Newell and Jane Doe days after the alleged incident, Jonathan apologizes to Jane and says, "You're an amazing person and I genuinely hope ur not catching as much heat from this as we r. We've been shutting down any stories we've heard but again I'm so so sorry."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            In another thread we obtained, accused former frat member Matthew Ingalls consoles Jane after she mentions having a UTI, and says of the rumors, "Stupid bitches like to yap, and the fact they're doing it shows that they're jealous of you for any number of reasons."
      
    
            The commission apologized to students who had planned to attend, saying Between Friends hopes to connect with local fans at a later date. It says it plans to organize a charity concert featuring local performers, including student bands and DJs, with all proceeds going to the Rape, Abuse & Incest National Network.
      
    
            The investigation into Jane Doe's case has been recently reopened by the Tompkins District Attorney.

schema.headline: Cornell University Cancels Homecoming Concert Amid Alleged Gang Rape Fallout
